WITH invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) as invoice_count
  FROM Invoices
  GROUP BY order_id
),
total_invoices_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(invoice_count) as total FROM invoice_counts
),
shares AS (
  SELECT 
    ic.order_id,
    ic.invoice_count,
    CAST(ic.invoice_count AS DECIMAL(19,4)) / CAST(tic.total AS DECIMAL(19,4)) as share
  FROM invoice_counts ic
  CROSS JOIN total_invoices_count tic
),
average_share_value AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share
  FROM shares
),
above_average_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    s.invoice_count,
    s.share
  FROM shares s
  CROSS JOIN average_share_value a
  WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
)
SELECT 
  SUM(invoice_count) as total_invoices,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share - (SELECT avg_share FROM average_share_value)) as avg_excess
FROM above_average_orders

assumptions.assumption: At least one order exists whose share is strictly above the overall average share. If no such orders exist, the query returns a row with NULL values (behavior varies by SQL dialect).
